Liberty CTI Open Source Analysis — For Texas Industry Situational Awareness UNCLASSIFIED // OPEN SOURCE // PROPRIETARY
DOJ/FBI seize platforms behind China’s QTFY hacking group, 26 Aug 2026, confirming 8 years of breaches across finance, telecom, DIB, and federal agencies — no victim list released Treasury unveils “Operation Economic Outcast” against Iran, 24 Aug 2026, then strips Banque Misr’s UAE branches of dollar access under Section 311, 28 Aug 2026 NSA/FBI/Cyber National Mission Force advisory names energy, water, finance, telecom, DIB, and higher education as QTFY-targeted sectors, 26 Aug 2026 DOJ/FBI seize platforms behind China’s QTFY hacking group, 26 Aug 2026, confirming 8 years of breaches across finance, telecom, DIB, and federal agencies — no victim list released Treasury unveils “Operation Economic Outcast” against Iran, 24 Aug 2026, then strips Banque Misr’s UAE branches of dollar access under Section 311, 28 Aug 2026 NSA/FBI/Cyber National Mission Force advisory names energy, water, finance, telecom, DIB, and higher education as QTFY-targeted sectors, 26 Aug 2026

Executive Warning: The Justice Department’s disruption of an eight-year Chinese state-sponsored hacking platform is this week’s central fact for Texas leadership — not a Washington story to file away. On 26 August, the FBI, NSA, and DOJ confirmed that the group known as QTFY had successfully breached financial institutions, defense contractors, telecommunications providers, and universities nationwide, alongside NASA, the Department of Justice, the Federal Reserve, and the Department of Energy, using a scanning-and-obfuscation platform that operated for years before this week’s seizure. No victim list has been released. Separately, Washington’s economic war against Iran escalated into a named, formal campaign layered with a new correspondent-banking weapon, even as diplomatic channels opened for the first time in weeks. Texas added its own thread when the Attorney General moved to restrict Chinese technology inside the state’s AI data centers, and ERCOT began the information requests that will decide the timeline for new grid capacity. The decision risk for executives: treating the China disruption as a federal cybersecurity story rather than an open question about their own network, when the federal government itself has not said who was hit.

Board Implications This Week — Ask

Have we independently hunted for the FBI/NSA-published QTFY indicators of compromise, or are we relying on the absence of our name from a victim list the government has not published?

Board Implications This Week — Direct

Direct Treasury/Finance to confirm OFAC and correspondent-banking screening is current against the 24 and 28 August Iran designations, including the new Section 311 mechanism now in active use against foreign banks.

Board Implications This Week — Document

Whatever the IT/security team finds — or does not find — in this week’s QTFY indicator hunt, put the scope, method, and result in board or risk-committee minutes now, while the tasking is fresh.

Board Implications This Week — Rehearse

Rehearse the decision you would face if a subpoena, regulator inquiry, or federal notification named your organization as a QTFY victim next month for intrusion activity that occurred years ago. Decide now who owns that conversation.

Dominant Judgment: An Eight-Year Chinese Access-Broker Network Reached Every Liberty CTI Priority Sector — And No Victim List Exists

It is a confirmed fact that the Department of Justice, FBI, NSA, and Cyber National Mission Force announced on 26 August 2026 the seizure of QScan and QTRouter — the scanning and traffic-obfuscation platforms behind QTFY (also tracked as QT or QTCYBER), a China state-sponsored group run through Nanjing Xinjiuwei Network Technology Company, staffed in part by former People’s Liberation Army personnel, and operating under contract to China’s Ministry of State Security since at least 2018. Federal court filings and the accompanying joint cybersecurity advisory confirm successful, completed breaches — not merely scans — of financial institutions, defense contractors, telecommunications providers, universities, and state governments, in addition to NASA, the Department of Justice, the Federal Reserve, and the Department of Energy. Separately disclosed unsuccessful attempts included a children’s hospital, a semiconductor company, a power company, the U.S. Senate, and election systems. The joint advisory names energy and power systems, water and wastewater, financial institutions, telecommunications, the defense industrial base, higher education, and federal civilian government as targeted sectors — precisely Liberty CTI’s five Texas priority sectors, plus water.

Liberty CTI assesses it is roughly even chance that additional Texas-headquartered organizations in financial services, energy, telecommunications, or the defense industrial base were among QTFY’s confirmed private-sector victims, though none has been publicly named as of this issue. This is a plausibility judgment, not a probability derived from evidence: it rests on the breadth of sectors named in the federal advisory, the campaign’s eight-year duration, and Texas’s outsized concentration in exactly those sectors — not on any Texas-specific finding. DOJ’s public materials withhold a victim list, and the takedown disrupts QTFY’s current tooling without confirming or ruling out any single organization’s prior exposure. The honest analytic position is that either outcome — Texas exposure or Texas exclusion — is about as likely as the other.

Bottom line: Executives should not wait for a subpoena or a federal notification to check. The FBI and NSA published indicators of compromise alongside the 26 August advisory specifically so organizations could look now — an eight-year-old access-broker network does not stop being a live question because its infrastructure was seized this week.

Section I

What Changed This Week

DOJ, FBI, and NSA Dismantle Eight-Year Chinese Access-Broker Network Spanning Every Liberty CTI Priority Sector

On 26 August 2026, the Justice Department announced court-authorized seizure of domains hard-coded into QScan (a distributed vulnerability-scanning and exploitation platform processing millions of tasks daily) and QTRouter (a traffic-obfuscation network built on compromised IoT devices), the core tools of the China state-sponsored group QTFY. The same day, NSA, FBI, and the Cyber National Mission Force published a joint cybersecurity advisory naming energy and power systems, water and wastewater, financial institutions, telecommunications, the defense industrial base, higher education, and federal civilian government as sectors QTFY targeted. Confirmed successful breaches include financial institutions, defense contractors, telecommunications providers, universities, state governments, NASA, the Department of Justice, the Federal Reserve, and the Department of Energy; confirmed unsuccessful attempts include a children’s hospital, a semiconductor company, a power company, the U.S. Senate, and election-system targets. No private-sector victim has been named, and Liberty CTI identified no Texas-specific confirmation as of this issue. The advisory includes indicators of compromise and directs organizations to hunt for them now rather than wait for notification.

Treasury Escalates Iran Economic War Under “Operation Economic Outcast,” Applies a New Correspondent-Banking Weapon

On 24 August 2026, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent unveiled “Operation Economic Outcast,” the detailed sanctions package anticipated in ATB-2026-24, expanding secondary sanctions across digital assets, technology, gold, aviation, and shipping, and designating nearly 60 entities, individuals, and vessels tied to Iranian nuclear/missile procurement, cyber operations, and oil smuggling. On 28 August, Treasury took its first correspondent-banking action under the campaign, proposing to strip the five UAE branches of Banque Misr — Egypt’s second-largest state-owned bank — of U.S. dollar correspondent access under Section 311 of the USA PATRIOT Act, citing roughly $1.8 billion in transactions linked to Iranian shadow-banking networks across 103 companies over two and a half years. OFAC added further Iran-related and counterterrorism designations on both 24 and 28 August. Analysts flagged a persistent enforcement gap: China, which routes an estimated 90 percent of Iranian oil exports, remains untouched by this round of measures.

Diplomatic Channels Reopen on the Strait of Hormuz, Even as the Waterway Stays Functionally Closed

The Strait of Hormuz remained closed to normal commercial traffic through the coverage window — only three ships transited on 23 August, against roughly 85 per day before the war — and U.S. and allied forces extended their pause on strikes against Iranian territory to 29 consecutive nights as of 28 August. Within that standoff, diplomatic activity intensified for the first time in weeks: a Pakistani military delegation led by army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir met Iranian officials on reopening the strait and reviving broader negotiations, characterized by Pakistan’s Interior Minister as “very positive and productive”; Qatar’s Prime Minister separately met four senior Iranian officials in Tehran; and an Iranian security official said the country is compiling a list of conditions for reopening the strait, including an end to the regional war. Brent crude fell 5.3 percent on the week, which Liberty CTI reads as markets pricing diplomatic momentum rather than a physical supply change. The underlying risk has not resolved: an unclaimed projectile struck a tanker off Oman’s coast on 24 August, disabling its engine with no casualties reported.

Texas Attorney General Moves to Restrict Chinese Technology in AI Data Centers

On 25 August, Attorney General Ken Paxton unveiled a four-point plan on AI data centers: calling for federal legislation to bar Chinese technology from data-center facilities; proposing criminal liability for AI chatbots that harm children; endorsing Governor Abbott’s existing pause on new interconnection approvals pending resource-use constraints; and stopping short of a moratorium on new projects. The announcement follows Abbott’s June directive requiring data centers to cover their own grid-infrastructure costs and his August audit order. The plan’s supply-chain premise — that Chinese-origin technology inside Texas AI infrastructure is itself a risk to be legislated against — lands in the same week federal authorities confirmed a Chinese state-sponsored group had breached telecommunications and defense-industrial targets nationally; Liberty CTI has identified no evidence tying the two directly, but the coincidence is analytically relevant to how Texas policymakers are likely to frame AI-infrastructure risk going forward.

ERCOT Opens First Round of Large-Load Information Requests Under December Audit Deadline

ERCOT began sending information requests to data-center operators in the Batch Zero process — roughly 300 data centers of 75 megawatts or larger — in the final days of August, with additional rounds expected through October and November, targeting completion of Governor Abbott’s audit directive by 10 December 2026. Separate community-impact reviews apply to data centers and crypto facilities of 25 megawatts or larger. ERCOT acknowledged its original April 2027 Batch Zero study deadline will not be met and that a revised timeline is under development; 17 large loads representing roughly 6.6 gigawatts of peak demand have already completed stability assessments and remain on track for late-2026 deployment regardless of the audit’s outcome.

Section II

Key Judgments

KJ-1
It is a confirmed fact that DOJ, FBI, NSA, and the Cyber National Mission Force disrupted the QTFY hacking platform on 26 August 2026 following at least eight years of activity, and that federal court filings and the joint advisory confirm successful breaches of financial institutions, defense contractors, telecommunications providers, universities, and state governments, in addition to federal civilian agencies. HIGH CONFIDENCE
Source basis: Department of Justice press release, 26 August 2026; NSA/FBI/Cyber National Mission Force joint cybersecurity advisory, 26 August 2026. Primary uncertainty: no complete victim list has been released; private-sector victim categories are confirmed, but individual organizations are not named.
Decision Implication: Every Texas organization in a named sector should run the published indicators of compromise this week, not wait for a notification that may never come.
KJ-2
Liberty CTI assesses it is roughly even chance that Texas-headquartered organizations are among QTFY’s unnamed private-sector victims, given the campaign’s eight-year duration, its confirmed reach into financial services, energy, telecommunications, and the defense industrial base nationally, and Texas’s concentration in exactly those sectors. LOW-MODERATE CONFIDENCE
Source basis: sector breadth disclosed in the 26 August joint advisory; Texas’s known concentration in defense-industrial, financial-services, and energy-sector activity as general background, not sourced to this week’s reporting. Primary uncertainty: this is an extrapolation from national sector-level disclosures with no Texas-specific anchor — the judgment could move sharply in either direction on the next indicator, and there is no evidentiary basis to lean toward exposure or toward exclusion.
Decision Implication: Do not read the absence of your organization’s name as evidence of exclusion, and do not read this judgment as a lean toward exposure. The operational action — run the indicators of compromise — does not change either way.
KJ-3
It is a confirmed fact that Treasury’s 24 August unveiling of Operation Economic Outcast and its 28 August Section 311 action against Banque Misr represent the detailed sanctions escalation ATB-2026-24 identified as pending, and that Pakistani- and Qatari-mediated diplomatic talks opened this week for the first time in the conflict as Brent crude fell 5.3%. Liberty CTI assesses with moderate confidence that this combination — harder sanctions paired with a genuine, if unconfirmed, diplomatic opening — modestly lowers near-term likelihood of Iran-attributed cyber escalation against Texas targets relative to ATB-2026-24’s rising-incentive judgment, though it does not eliminate that risk while sanctions pressure continues to build. MODERATE CONFIDENCE
Source basis: Treasury/Axios/NPR reporting on the 24 August Bessent announcement; ofac.treasury.gov/recent-actions, 24 and 28 August 2026; open-source conflict tracking for strait-transit and diplomatic reporting, 27–28 August 2026. Primary uncertainty: no government source has confirmed Iran’s underlying intentions; the diplomatic signals are Iranian and mediator statements, not a verified change in Tehran’s cyber posture.
Decision Implication: Continue OT/ICS patching and OFAC-screening discipline as before — this is a moderation of urgency, not a stand-down.
Section III

Geopolitical Driver

Two nation-state threads dominate this week, and they point in different directions. China’s QTFY disruption is the clearer of the two: a confirmed, multi-year, multi-sector access-broker campaign that reached exactly the sectors Liberty CTI tracks for Texas, disrupted only after eight years of operation. Iran presents a more ambiguous picture — economic pressure is intensifying by the day (Operation Economic Outcast, the Banque Misr correspondent-banking action) even as diplomatic channels opened for the first time since the conflict began, with Pakistan and Qatar both engaged as mediators and Iran reportedly drafting reopening conditions for the strait. Russia and DPRK remain standing watch items. On DPRK specifically: a Lazarus Group kernel-level Windows exploit (CVE-2026-68820), deployed via fake job offers targeting defense and aerospace workers under the long-running “Operation Dream Job,” carried a federal patch-compliance deadline of 25 August 2026 under Binding Operational Directive 26-04 — a continuation of the DIB-targeting campaign Liberty CTI has tracked since ATB-2026-23, not a new development, but a concrete near-term compliance date DIB contractors should confirm they met. No new indicator ties either Russia or DPRK directly to a Texas target this week.

Continuum assessment: Texas remains in competition, sharpened by confirmed nation-state access-broker exposure. The QTFY disruption converts a background assumption — that Chinese state-sponsored actors target U.S. critical infrastructure — into a confirmed, sector-specific fact with no Texas exclusion available. The Iran thread shifts modestly toward diplomatic uncertainty rather than pure escalation. No Flash Warning threshold was met this week.

Section IV

Why This Matters to Texas

No Texas organization has been named as a QTFY victim, and no Iran-attributed action struck a Texas target this week. Neither fact should read as reassurance. QTFY’s victim list is confirmed to include financial institutions, defense contractors, telecommunications providers, and universities nationally — sectors in which Texas holds an outsized share of the national base — and the government has not said which specific organizations, in which states, were breached. Separately, Texas’s own AI-governance response (the Paxton plan) and grid-capacity process (ERCOT’s RFIs) both advanced this week on their own institutional timelines, independent of any single incident. The throughline across all four developments is the same one Liberty CTI has flagged before: Texas exposure this week is a function of sector concentration and infrastructure dependency, not of any single confirmed local attack.

Cross-Sector Cascade Assessment

Energy
ERCOT / OT / Grid Capacity
What changed: The 26 August QTFY advisory names energy and power systems as a targeted sector, with one power company disclosed as an unsuccessful target nationally; ERCOT began Batch Zero large-load information requests toward its 10 December audit deadline; the Strait of Hormuz remains functionally closed but Brent crude fell 5.3% on diplomatic movement. Why it matters locally: Texas energy and utility operators sit inside a confirmed nation-state targeting set for the first time this cycle with hard sector attribution, not an inferred one, while ERCOT’s audit timeline continues to shape 2027 capacity planning independent of any single incident. Cascade risk: Any Texas energy or utility operator should run the QTFY indicators of compromise this week alongside any still-open Siemens S7 patching from prior issues; large-load operators should confirm their RFI response is tracking ERCOT’s schedule rather than assuming automatic inclusion in the 17 already-cleared loads.
Financial
Nation-State Exposure / OFAC Screening
What changed: The QTFY advisory confirms successful breaches of financial institutions nationally, alongside the Federal Reserve; separately, Treasury’s Operation Economic Outcast and its first Section 311 correspondent-banking action against Banque Misr sharply raise the bar for OFAC and correspondent-banking screening currency. Why it matters locally: Texas financial institutions face a two-track exposure this week — a confirmed nation-state access-broker campaign that has already breached peer institutions nationally, and an expanding, faster-moving sanctions regime that can sever a bank’s own dollar access if screening lags. Cascade risk: Any Texas bank, credit union, or energy financier with Gulf-adjacent correspondent relationships should confirm screening is current against the 24 and 28 August designations this week; the Section 311 mechanism used against Banque Misr is designed to scale to additional institutions quickly.
Healthcare / DIB / AI
Supply-Chain Risk / State AI Governance
What changed: QTFY confirmed breaches of defense contractors, telecommunications providers, and universities, with an unsuccessful attempt against a children’s hospital; separately, the DPRK’s Operation Dream Job campaign carried a 25 August federal patch deadline for defense/aerospace targets (CVE-2026-68820); and Texas’s Attorney General moved this week to restrict Chinese technology inside AI data centers. Why it matters locally: the defense-industrial base and higher-education sectors named in the QTFY advisory are core to San Antonio and Texas’s broader DIB footprint, and the new state AI-governance push signals that supply-chain origin — not just technical vulnerability — is becoming a Texas regulatory concern. Cascade risk: DIB contractors should confirm CVE-2026-68820 patch compliance and run the QTFY indicators of compromise in the same pass; AI-infrastructure operators should track the Paxton plan’s federal-legislation ask, since it would directly affect vendor and hardware sourcing decisions if enacted.
Section V

Indicators & Warnings — PIR Watch, 1 to 4 Weeks

PIR 4 / I&W 1 A named Texas victim in the QTFY campaign ↑ Rising
  • Watch for a DOJ court filing, breach-notification disclosure, or state attorney general filing naming a Texas-headquartered financial institution, energy company, telecommunications provider, or defense contractor as a confirmed QTFY victim.
  • Would convert this week’s national, sector-level exposure judgment into a confirmed Texas-specific finding.
  • Tied to: PIR 4, business-impact scenarios affecting operations and continuity.
PIR 3 / I&W 2 Additional Section 311 correspondent-banking actions ↑ Rising
  • Watch for Treasury applying the Section 311 mechanism used against Banque Misr to additional foreign financial institutions, which would broaden and accelerate correspondent-banking and OFAC-adjacent compliance obligations for any Texas bank with Gulf-region exposure.
  • Tied to: PIR 3, escalation indicators.
PIR 1 / I&W 3 Formal terms or timeline for reopening the Strait of Hormuz → Unclear
  • Watch for Iran to formally publish reopening conditions following the Pakistani- and Qatari-mediated talks, or alternatively for a resumption of kinetic activity that would end the current 29-night pause.
  • Either outcome would materially reprice energy costs and shipping-insurance premiums for Texas Gulf Coast operators within days.
  • Tied to: PIR 1, adversary intent and geopolitical trigger indicators.
PIR 4 / I&W 4 ERCOT Batch Zero RFI results and audit timeline → Sustained
  • Watch for the first round of ERCOT large-load information-request responses and whether reporting tracks toward the 10 December audit-completion target or slips further, given ERCOT’s own acknowledgment that the original 2027 study deadline will not hold.
  • Continuation of PIR 4 carried from ATB-2026-24, which watched for the RFIs to open; they opened this week, and the indicator now escalates to their results.
  • Tied to: PIR 4, business and operational continuity exposure.
PIR 7 / I&W 5 Movement on Paxton’s AI data-center plan → Unclear
  • Watch for whether Paxton’s call for federal legislation restricting Chinese technology in data centers gains a congressional sponsor, and whether Texas legislators introduce a state-level companion measure ahead of any 2027 session.
  • Would directly affect vendor and hardware sourcing decisions for any Texas AI-infrastructure operator.
  • Tied to: PIR 7, decision-readiness and regulatory-exposure indicators.
Section VI

Governance Implication Block

Decision at risk
Whether the organization has independently verified — rather than assumed from the absence of a public victim list — that it was not compromised or scanned by QTFY’s QScan/QTRouter infrastructure, and whether OFAC and correspondent-banking screening are current against Treasury’s expanding Section 311 designations.
Owner
CISO/CIO for the QTFY indicator-of-compromise hunt and any carried-forward OT/ICS patching. CFO/Treasury/General Counsel for OFAC and Section 311 correspondent-banking exposure. Board risk committee for oversight of both.
Consequence of delay
An organization that waits for a public victim list before checking its own environment may already be compromised and simply undetected — QTFY operated for eight years before this week’s disruption. A financial institution with stale Section 311 screening risks losing its own correspondent access, not only its counterparty’s.
Action this week
Direct IT/security to run the FBI/NSA-published QTFY indicators of compromise against your environment now. Confirm with CFO/Treasury that OFAC and correspondent-banking screening are current against the 24 and 28 August Iran designations. If your organization is a defense-industrial contractor, confirm CVE-2026-68820 patch compliance against the 25 August federal deadline.
Record to preserve
Documentation of the QTFY indicator hunt, its scope, and its result, regardless of outcome. OFAC/Section 311 screening review date and findings. Patch-compliance record for CVE-2026-68820. Any board or risk-committee minutes reflecting this week’s tasking.
From Warning to Decision

Would your leadership team act in time?

Reading the warning is one thing. Making the decision with incomplete information and the clock running is another.

Section VII

Actions This Week

Ask: If our organization were among QTFY’s unnamed victims, would we know it today — or only when the government tells us?

Approve: An immediate, documented hunt for the published QTFY indicators of compromise across the environment, regardless of sector, this week.

Document: The scope and outcome of that hunt, plus this week’s OFAC/Section 311 screening review, in board or risk-committee minutes.

Rehearse: How the organization would respond if named as a QTFY victim in a future filing for activity that occurred years ago — decide now who leads that response.

Section VIII

Prior Judgment Tracker

Prior judgment
ATB-2026-24 assessed, at moderate confidence, that Washington’s shift to declared economic warfare against Iran raised Tehran’s incentive to activate pre-positioned cyber and industrial-control access as sanctions began to bite.
Current status
Moderated, not reversed. The anticipated detailed sanctions package landed as expected (Operation Economic Outcast, 24 August), but rather than an accompanying Iran-attributed cyber escalation, this week brought the first diplomatic opening of the conflict — Pakistani and Qatari mediation, and Iranian signals of draft reopening conditions. No Iran-attributed cyber action against a Texas target was identified this week.
What changed
This week’s dominant new development was not Iran-related at all: the confirmed, eight-year Chinese QTFY access-broker campaign, disrupted 26 August, is a new and separate judgment thread that did not exist in ATB-2026-24. The UTSA/Texas Cyber Command thread carried from ATB-2026-24 is largely closed for this issue: classes resumed on schedule 24 August with more than 42,000 students, and no further public update on the forensic investigation’s conclusions was identified this week.
Confidence movement
ATB-2026-24’s Iran cyber-incentive judgment moves from moderate confidence toward the lower end of that band, given this week’s diplomatic signals, without being retired. A new judgment is introduced this issue at high confidence (KJ-1) on the confirmed facts of the QTFY takedown, and at moderate confidence (KJ-2) on Texas-specific exposure.
Next indicator
A named Texas victim in the QTFY campaign, a formal Iranian reopening timeline for the Strait of Hormuz, or an additional Section 311 correspondent-banking action would each move posture in these threads going forward.

// Torch Fusion Cycle — ATB-2026-25

WHAT: The week of 23–29 August 2026 was defined by DOJ’s disruption of the eight-year Chinese QTFY access-broker network (26 August), Treasury’s escalation to “Operation Economic Outcast” against Iran with a first-of-its-kind Section 311 correspondent-banking action (24 and 28 August), a genuine diplomatic opening on the Strait of Hormuz, Texas AG Paxton’s AI data-center plan (25 August), and ERCOT’s first Batch Zero information requests. WHO: DOJ, FBI, NSA, and the Cyber National Mission Force; U.S. Treasury/OFAC; Pakistani and Qatari mediators; Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton; and ERCOT defined this week’s evidence base. WHY: An eight-year-old nation-state access-broker network reaching every Liberty CTI priority sector, disclosed without a victim list, is precisely the kind of change that should move an executive from passive awareness to an active check of their own environment. WHAT NEXT: Watch for a named Texas victim in the QTFY campaign, a formal Iranian reopening timeline for the strait, and further Section 311 correspondent-banking actions. The task this week is not to wait for the government to say who was hit — the published indicators of compromise are actionable now. Warnings that arrive too late are not warnings. They are after-action reports.
